notes_for_questioner: Minor wording points for the editor (not blocking): (1) 'S is a false negative for the AGN' over-reads it: S is a low-luminosity AGN with a small bolometric fraction, and the Nishimura sample shows no ratio-alpha_AGN link, so the diagnostic is not expected to flag it; say 'S gives no AGN signature' instead. (2) Nishimura's sample is built around HCN-vib/CON searches of buried nuclei, so it is not a neutral LIRG baseline; the CON flags (Table 1 col. 8) were garbled and the asterisks mark 'not in Paper I', not CON. A CON vs non-CON split could be done from Falstad+2021/Paper I and would address the 'CON-like?' part of the question; list as open. (3) The aperture definition differs (Nishimura: one beam on the nucleus; ours: moment-0 within beam, +-350 km/s), and ratios at 55 pc vs 250 pc (0.99 vs 0.69) both should be quoted, since N is mid-range at 55 pc but only 19th percentile at 250 pc. New question: an N-core at 0.99 inside 30 pc rising to ~1 is within the range seen in HCN-vib CONs; does N show HCN-vib (already a project test) and does Nishimura's resolved/global enhancement correlate with HCN-vib detection?
